messages.content: You are an experienced power-plant performance engineer. Answer with a single JSON object and nothing else.

A combined cycle power plant has one gas turbine, a heat recovery steam generator and a steam turbine. It runs at full load. Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has no inlet air conditioning, and over this ambient range the gas turbine stays below the rated limit of its generator. The plant has no inlet anti-icing system.

Question: over the 2 to 37 degC ambient range, is there a temperature beyond which the net output responds to ambient temperature differently from elsewhere? There may be none, one or more on the cold side, one on the hot side, or several.
Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"boundaries": [{"side": "below" or "above", "at_c": <degC>, "rh_above": <percent, or null>, "mechanism": "power_cap" or "anti_icing" or "evap_cooling" or "other", "response_beyond": "weaker" or "near_zero" or "opposite" or "same_or_stronger", "confidence": <0 to 1>}], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}
"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling. "response_beyond" compares how net output responds to ambient temperature beyond at_c with how it responds elsewhere in the range: weaker = same direction but a clearly smaller change per degC; near_zero = output barely changes with ambient temperature; opposite = output changes in the opposite direction; same_or_stronger = same direction and at least as large a change per degC. Use an empty list if you expect no such temperature.
You are an experienced power-plant performance engineer. Answer with a single JSON object and nothing else.

A combined cycle power plant has one gas turbine, a heat recovery steam generator and a steam turbine. It runs at full load. A combined cycle power plant has one gas turbine, a heat recovery steam generator and a steam turbine. It runs at full load. Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has an inlet evaporative cooler in front of the compressor, which operators run in warm weather. In cold weather the gas turbine reaches the rated limit of its generator, and the control system holds it at that limit. The plant has no inlet anti-icing system. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. The gas turbine generator is limited to 364 MW. Operators switch the evaporative cooler on when ambient temperature exceeds about 24 degC.

On cold, humid days an inlet anti-icing system heats the intake air with compressor bleed. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. Anti-icing keeps the compressor inlet at about 7 degC when relative humidity is above about 70%.

Question: over the 2 to 37 degC ambient range, is there a temperature beyond which the net output responds to ambient temperature differently from elsewhere? There may be none, one or more on the cold side, one on the hot side, or several.
Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"boundaries": [{"side": "below" or "above", "at_c": <degC>, "rh_above": <percent, or null>, "mechanism": "power_cap" or "anti_icing" or "evap_cooling" or "other", "response_beyond": "weaker" or "near_zero" or "opposite" or "same_or_stronger", "confidence": <0 to 1>}], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}
"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling. "response_beyond" compares how net output responds to ambient temperature beyond at_c with how it responds elsewhere in the range: weaker = same direction but a clearly smaller change per degC; near_zero = output barely changes with ambient temperature; opposite = output changes in the opposite direction; same_or_stronger = same direction and at least as large a change per degC. Use an empty list if you expect no such temperature.
